top_cluster.headline: The Senate Homeland Security Committee, led by Sen. Rand Paul with subcommittee work by Sen. Ron Johnson, is voting on whether to hold Dr. Anthony Fauci in contempt of Congress after he invoked his Fifth Amendment right in a hearing, while investigators separately obtained a forensic copy of his HHS-era iPhone.
top_cluster.left_framing: Left and center-left outlets emphasize institutional process and Republican aggression — describing a GOP senator's pursuit of Fauci's personal device and a politically charged committee vote — while giving space to Fauci's legal rationale (Fifth Amendment) and framing the inquiry's motives as contested rather than assuming guilt.
top_cluster.center_framing: NPR and PBS frame the story narrowly as a constitutional/procedural question — focused on the mechanics and legality of the contempt vote and Fifth Amendment invocation — without assigning blame to either Fauci or the committee.
top_cluster.right_framing: Right and far-right outlets emphasize escalating accountability and suspicion, portraying Fauci as evasive through repeated references to his Fifth Amendment invocations, the seizure of his phone, and (on Breitbart) an expanding web of congressional and state investigations, implying prior misconduct.
top_cluster.left_omissions: Left-leaning coverage omits the broader investigative context that Breitbart includes, such as state-level attorney general probes and characterization of the phone extraction as a formal 'forensic' procedure, details that lend a more severe, wrongdoing-implying cast to the story.
top_cluster.right_omissions: Right-leaning coverage omits Fauci's stated legal justification for invoking the Fifth Amendment and does not present the committee's motives as potentially political, details centered outlets and the Washington Post include to contextualize his non-cooperation as a legal defense rather than evasion.

blindspot_narrative: Right-leaning outlets are conspicuously silent on the DOJ-Epstein withholding lawsuit despite the topic's historical salience to their audience — a silence that only makes sense if the target (a Trump-appointed Acting AG) makes the story inconvenient. Left-leaning outlets, meanwhile, are underplaying how much establishment and pro-Israel money was deployed against El-Sayed, protecting a clean 'grassroots progressive win' narrative at the cost of a messier intra-party financial story. In both cases, the avoided detail is the one that complicates each side's preferred hero/villain framing.
